messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: inference-pool-us-west1 queue growth > 5k, P99 latency spiking, autoscaler throttled at max_nodes. Alert ID 2026-03-15-AP1

sre-oncall: I'm on it. Acknowledge. Getting current autoscale state and queue tail logs.

runtime-ops: seeing sustained queue length across grpc-router. Autoscaler shows max 85/85 nodes, scale attempt throttled due to global quota check. Lots of small free slices but can't place new pods.

ml-serving: customer-facing spikes started ~ 02:13 UTC — 503s and retries for streaming endpoints for two enterprise tenants. CS notified?

cust-success: yes, CS has two tickets open (C-1122, C-1123). Notifying customers that we're investigating.

product-pd: impact tier? estimated % of request loss? need blunt messaging for the status page.

ml-serving: rough numbers from logs: ~7% error rate on generation API for those tenants, retries masked some errors. Latency p50 -> p95 jumped x6.

infra-eng: attaching a quick snapshot: node pools have mixed MIG configs. Some instances are A100 with 4-slice MIG, others 1-slice. Scheduler can't pack heterogeneous slices efficiently -> a lot of 0.5-1 GPU free per node effectively unusable for current pod profiles.

sre-oncall: that sounds like fragmentation/packing problem, not pure quota. Can you confirm whether the autoscaler refused due to reaching node limit or couldn't find fit for pending pods?

runtime-ops: checking pending pods: many pending are inference-worker pods requesting 0.5 GPU equivalent (we request device plugin fractional requests). The scheduler logs show "NoCapacity" for gpu resources even though aggregate free GPU <-> pending demand mismatch.

infra-eng: yep. Example: 20 nodes with 0.25+0.25 free slices scattered; scheduling binpacking can't combine slices across MIG granularity. Also observed MIG size mismatch: some nodes use 7g.5gb slices vs others with big monolithic slices.

ml-serving: quick repro snippets from scheduler logs:

```
I0315 02:16:12.123 kube-scheduler schedule.go: pod inference-worker-abc: binding failed: failed to find fit: resource shortage: gpu-mig/1 not found
I0315 02:16:12.124 kubelet kubelet.go: can't allocate device: requested 0.5, node has 1x0.5 fragmented across two MIG profiles
```

runtime-ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) emergency autoscale override to allow new node types (bump max), 2) trigger repack job that consolidates fractional workloads onto a subset of nodes and drains others, 3) migrate low-priority batch to a different pool.

sre-oncall: prefer non-breaking; what's lowest risk?

runtime-ops: lowest risk = migrate batch workloads off the inference pool and kick a repack to defragment. But repack needs nodes to be cordoned and drained which temporarily reduces capacity. So combine with temporary max increase to reduce impact.

product-pd: we need a short customer-facing blurb: "Experiencing degraded performance due to capacity placement issues; engineers are actively rebalancing capacity. Customers may see intermittent 503s." Approve?

cust-success: approve. Posting now.

deploy-bot: /scale autoscaler inference-pool-us-west1 --max 110 --note "emergency surge override"

infra-eng: override applied, max set to 110. New node request accepted but scheduling still finding fragmented slices. New nodes will help but packing must be improved.

runtime-ops: starting repack job (packer-v2) targeting pool inference-pool-us-west1. Plan: cordon 10 low-util nodes, drain pods, allow packer to reschedule pods to denser nodes, then terminate emptied nodes. Running in dry-run first then live.

sre-oncall: please post command you run so I can follow:

```
# cordon + drain target nodes list
kubectl cordon gpu-node-45
kubectl drain gpu-node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# start repack controller
kubectl apply -f repack-job.yaml
```

runtime-ops: dry-run shows ~40% of pods can be consolidated; live run in 2m. Starting now.

ml-serving: monitoring customer error rate. If repack causes short term request drops we'll reroute heavy customers to standby region if needed.

sre-oncall: do we have standby capacity in us-east or dedicated dedicated pools to failover customers?

product-pd: two affected customers have org-level failover enabled but not turned on automatically. Discussing with CS to flip for them if we hit another threshold.

runtime-ops: repack live: cordoned 10 nodes. Draining... some pods evicted, new pods scheduled to higher density nodes. Observed momentary spike in CPU but GPU allocation improved.

deploy-bot: Autoscaler activity: scaled up by +12 nodes in the last 4m. New nodes joining.

infra-eng: repack + scale combined trimmed fragmentation: we freed ~18 GPU slices effectively (estimate). Pending queue dropped from 5k -> 900 in 8m.

ml-serving: customer error rate dropping to 1.2% now. p95 latency trending down. CS: update sent to customers that we're seeing recovery.

cust-success: customers acknowledged and appreciate the update. No cancellation requests so far.

sre-oncall: current status: queue still above baseline but steadily decreasing. Keeping pager open for next 60m. Who owns postmortem?

runtime-ops: runtime-ops will own the incident PM; initial RCA: MIG/instance mix caused binpacking failure under surge; autoscaler hit pre-configured node max and scheduler couldn't fit fractional GPU requests. Action items: 1) review MIG sizing and standardize slice profiles, 2) improve scheduler preemption/packing heuristics, 3) repack automation during surge, 4) revisit autoscale default max thresholds and surge quotas.

product-pd: schedule a follow-up meeting 48h. Assign owners and write customer incident summary.

infra-eng: short-term: add automated repack trigger when pending queue > 2k for >5m. Medium-term: migrate to uniform MIG profiles per pool.

sre-oncall: thanks everyone. Leaving detailed logs and timing in incident tracker. Marking page resolved for now but watching. :thumbsup:

runtime-ops: post-ops note: repack completed, terminated 8 nodes, freed capacity, autoscaler scaled back to 90 over 30m. Follow-up ticket created: INF-2248 (MIG profile harmonization).

deploy-bot: Incident closed by runtime-ops.

cust-success: closing customer tickets with summary.

runtime-ops: postmortem owner: runtime-ops, due in 48h. Will include timeline, command log, and suggested config changes.

sre-oncall: final note - if you were paged, please ack in the rotation log and file any oncall followups.

incident-bot: Incident 4481234567 closed. Duration: 00:47:22. Severity: Sev2.
